title: AI Fairness 360: An extensible toolkit for detecting and mitigating algorithmic bias
venue: IBM Journal of Research and Development
abstract: Fairness is an increasingly important concern as machine learning models are used to support decision making in high-stakes applications such as mortgage lending, hiring, and prison sentencing. This article introduces a new open-source Python toolkit for algorithmic fairness, AI Fairness 360 (AIF360), released under an Apache v2.0 license (https://github.com/ibm/aif360). The main objectives of this toolkit are to help facilitate the transition of fairness research algorithms for use in an industrial setting and to provide a common framework for fairness researchers to share and evaluate algorithms. The package includes a comprehensive set of fairness metrics for datasets and models, explanations for these metrics, and algorithms to mitigate bias in datasets and models. It also includes an interactive Web experience that provides a gentle introduction to the concepts and capabilities for line-of-business users, researchers, and developers to extend the toolkit with their new algorithms and improvements and to use it for performance benchmarking. A built-in testing infrastructure maintains code quality.

claims.text: AI Fairness 360 (AIF360) is an open-source Python toolkit for algorithmic fairness released under an Apache v2.0 license.
AIF360 provides fairness metrics for datasets and machine learning models.
AIF360 provides explanations for fairness metrics.
AIF360 provides algorithms to mitigate algorithmic bias in datasets and models.
AIF360 includes an interactive Web experience to introduce concepts and capabilities to users.
AIF360 includes a built-in testing infrastructure to maintain code quality.
AI Fairness 360 provides over 71 bias detection metrics, 9 bias mitigation algorithms, and a metric explanations facility in a Python package conforming to scikit-learn conventions.
Reweighing and optimized pre-processing algorithms improve statistical parity difference and disparate impact metrics across Adult, German Credit, and COMPAS datasets.
Applying the Reweighing pre-processor on the Adult dataset test partition reduces the statistical parity difference from -0.2021 to -0.0119.
Reject option classification substantially improves fairness metrics on the Adult dataset but causes a significant reduction in classification accuracy.

limitations.text: It is mathematically impossible to satisfy all definitions of fairness at the same time.
The least improvement in fairness metrics was observed on the German Credit dataset, likely due to its small size of 1,000 records.
Reject option classification post-processing is brittle and causes significant reductions in accuracy.
The current web service backend is limited to three built-in datasets and logistic regression classifiers.
The toolkit's metrics and algorithms focus primarily on distributive justice and do not capture all aspects or full scope of fairness.

future_work.text: Expand the toolkit to measure and mitigate other aspects of justice such as compensatory justice.
Extend the variety of types of explanations offered and create guidance for practitioners on when specific explanation types are most appropriate.
Expand the web application service to support user dataset uploads and additional classifier models.
